title: Demo paper — every question type in one sitting
scope: Every question type, media block and marking rule the panel supports
provenance: bundled demo, written for this plugin — not a previous-year paper. Delete it once you have sourced a real one.

questions.text: Which organelle is the main site of ATP synthesis in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, 20% of the bases are guanine. What percentage of the bases are adenine?
questions.explanation: G = C, so C is also 20% and G+C = 40%; the remaining 60% splits equally, A = T = 30%. Short numeric options like these are legitimate answers — the lint guard rejects debris, never brevity.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: Which amino acid carries a net positive charge at physiological pH?
questions.explanation: Lysine's side-chain amine stays protonated (pKa ~10.5) at pH 7.4; aspartate is negative, alanine and serine are neutral.

media.text: Assume standard side-chain pKₐ values and pH 7.4.

questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin — carries a text-note media block

questions.text: Select every component of a nucleotide.
questions.explanation: A nucleotide is sugar + base + phosphate; amino acids build proteins, not nucleotides. MSQ grades on the exact set — any missing or extra tick is wrong, and this section carries no negative marking (GATE-style).
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: The table lists four restriction enzymes and where each cuts inside its recognition site. Which of them leave blunt ends?
questions.explanation: A cut in the middle of a palindromic site (SmaI CCC^GGG, HaeIII GG^CC) leaves flush blunt ends; the staggered cuts of EcoRI and HindIII leave single-stranded overhangs — sticky ends.

media.caption: ^ marks the phosphodiester bond cut on the strand shown (5′→3′).

questions.text: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human somatic cell?
questions.explanation: 23 pairs: 22 autosomal pairs plus one sex chromosome pair. The field here is declared 'integer' — digits only, no decimal point.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: An aqueous solution contains 0.05 M of a strong monoprotic acid. What is its pH? (round to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: $$\text{pH} = -\log_{10}[\text{H}^+] = -\log_{10}(0.05) \approx 1.30$$ The key carries a tolerance ($\pm\, 0.05$), so 1.3 and 1.30 both grade correct.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: A bacterial culture grows from 10² to 10⁸ cells in 6 hours. What is its mean doubling time, in minutes? (round to one decimal)
questions.explanation: Generations = log₂(10⁶) ≈ 19.93; 360 min ÷ 19.93 ≈ 18.1 min. Real keys state a range for such answers, so this one is stored the GATE way: midpoint 18 with tolerance 0.5. With no declared input, the decimal field is inferred from the key and the prompt.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: What is the term for the programmed, gene-directed death of a cell? Answer with one word, in lowercase — grading matches the text exactly.
questions.explanation: Apoptosis. This field accepts any text; grading is an exact string match, so the paper states the expected form.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: The figure shows growth of the same bacterial strain in two cultures, A at 37 °C and B at 25 °C. Which conclusion does the figure support?
options: Culture B grows faster than culture A throughout the experiment.
Culture B never enters exponential growth.
Culture B has a longer lag phase but reaches the same final density as culture A.
Culture A reaches a higher stationary-phase density than culture B.
questions.explanation: B's rise starts about 3–4 h later than A's (longer lag), but both curves flatten on the same dotted line at OD₆₀₀ ≈ 1.0 — the stationary density is equal, B's slope never exceeds A's, and B clearly passes through exponential growth.

media.alt: Two sigmoid growth curves on one pair of axes: curve A (37 °C) begins rising around 2 h and curve B (25 °C) around 5 h; both flatten at OD600 ≈ 1.0
media.caption: Growth of one strain at 37 °C (A) and 25 °C (B); the dotted line marks OD₆₀₀ = 1.0.

questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin — figure generated for this paper

questions.text: The four curves show initial velocity v against substrate concentration [S] for the same enzyme under four conditions; exactly one condition includes an inhibitor. Which curve shows competitive inhibition?
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibition raises apparent Km without changing Vmax: curve B plateaus at the same height as the uninhibited curve A but needs more substrate to get there. Curve C plateaus lower (non-competitive, Vmax halved); curve D is sigmoidal (cooperative kinetics), not Michaelis–Menten at all. Every option carries its own figure — option-level media.

option_media.alt: Curve A: a hyperbola rising steeply and plateauing at v ≈ 1.0 by [S] ≈ 5 mM
Curve B: a hyperbola rising more gradually than A, reaching the same plateau at v ≈ 1.0 only near [S] ≈ 10 mM
Curve C: a hyperbola that plateaus at half the height of A, at v ≈ 0.5
Curve D: a sigmoidal curve, flat below [S] ≈ 0.5 mM and steeper than a hyperbola around its midpoint

questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin — option figures generated for this paper

questions.text: Colony counts from a serial dilution are shown in the figure. A plate is countable when it carries 30–300 colonies. How many colony-forming units per mL were in the ORIGINAL sample? (whole number)
questions.explanation: Plate 3 (10⁻³) holds 120 colonies — the only countable plate (450 is over 300, 12 is under 30). 120 × 10³ = 1.2 × 10⁵ = 120000 CFU/mL. A free-entry question can ride on a figure, and 'whole number' in the prompt makes this field digits-only; a nat never takes a penalty, so this question overrides the section's −0.67 with 0.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin — figure generated for this paper

questions.text: Which of the following sugars is a ketose?
questions.explanation: Fructose is a ketohexose; glucose, galactose and ribose are aldoses.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: A solution's absorbance is measured within the linear range of the Beer–Lambert law, $A = \varepsilon\, c\, l$. What happens to the absorbance $A$ if the analyte concentration $c$ is doubled?
questions.explanation: $A = \varepsilon c\, l$ is linear in $c$, so doubling the concentration doubles the absorbance. The question overrides the section's marking to 1 mark correct / −0.33 wrong; the same section carries 2-mark questions beside it.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: Which of the following are components of a standard PCR mix?
questions.explanation: The mix is buffer + Mg²⁺, dNTPs, primers and Taq. Ethidium bromide stains gels after the run — it is never part of the reaction mix.
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin

questions.text: How many ATP molecules does glycolysis yield NET per molecule of glucose?
questions.explanation: Four ATP are made, two are invested in the priming steps — net 2. Like E-02, this one is worth 1 mark (override), and only the first 3 saved answers in this section are graded (attempt limit 3 of 4).
questions.provenance: bundled demo question, written for this plugin
